title: Promises made in a crisis
odia: ଆତଙ୍କ ବେଳେ ଯାଚନ୍ତି କୁକୁଡ଼ା, ଆତଙ୍କ ଗଲେ ଦିଅନ୍ତି ନେଫେଡ଼ା
literal_meaning: In a crisis they promise a chicken; when the crisis passes they give “ନେଫେଡ଼ା” (the final noun is left untranslated because its meaning is unresolved here).
explanation: The source explains this as a vow made to God during danger and neglected once the danger passes. More broadly, it can remind someone not to forget a promise after receiving help. The precise meaning of the final noun is unresolved; the interpretation follows the supplied gloss.
meaning_odia: ବିପଦରେ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ମାନସିକ କରାଗଲା, ବିପଦ ଟଳିଲା ପରେ ସେହି କଥା ଭୁଲିଗଲେ—ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏହି ଆଚରଣକୁ ଧରେ। ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ଦରକାର ବେଳର ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ଓ ସ୍ୱସ୍ତି ମିଳିବା ପରର ବ୍ୟବହାର ମେଳ ଖାଉଛି କି ନାହିଁ, ସେହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଏଥିରୁ ଉଠେ। ଶେଷ ଶବ୍ଦ ‘ନେଫେଡ଼ା’ର ସଠିକ୍ ଅର୍ଥ ଏଠାରେ ଅନିଶ୍ଚିତ; ଏହି ବୁଝାମଣା ଉତ୍ସର ଦିଆଯାଇଥିବା ଅର୍ଥ ଉପରେ ନିର୍ଭର କରେ।
usage_example: After asking for urgent help and promising to return it, someone stops answering once their own problem is solved. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The religious vow is the source’s explanatory setting, not a recommendation or a claim that everyone follows this practice. A previously deferred dictionary saying has different wording; no equivalence or repaired final word is certified.

title: The words will outlast the moment
literal_meaning: The words will remain for all time.
explanation: A conversation ends, but what was said can remain in memory. The dictionary labels this short line a Dhaga under “for ever”. It can give a promise weight or warn that a remark will not be easily forgotten. Which feeling it carries depends on the speaker and the occasion; the source does not specify a single original scene.
meaning_odia: କଥା କହିବାର ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତଟି ସରିଯାଏ, ହେଲେ କହିଥିବା କଥା ମନରେ ରହିଯାଇପାରେ। ଛୋଟ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଗୋଟିଏ ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତିକୁ ଓଜନ ଦେଇପାରେ, ପୁଣି ଭୁଲି ନ ହେବା ଭଳି କଥା ପ୍ରତି ସତର୍କ କରିପାରେ। କିଏ କାହାକୁ କେଉଁ ସ୍ୱରରେ କହୁଛି, ସେଥିରୁ ଏହାର ଭାବ ବଦଳେ।
english_summary: A conversation ends, but what was said can remain in memory.
odia_summary: କଥା କହିବାର ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତଟି ସରିଯାଏ, ହେଲେ କହିଥିବା କଥା ମନରେ ରହିଯାଇପାରେ।
usage_example: Two friends recall a promise made years earlier; one says that the words have stayed with them. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)

odia: ପୂରୂବ କହ୍ନେଇ କି? ଲହୁଣିଆଁ ମାଠ କାନ୍ଧରେ ପଡିଲେ, ମଣିଷ ଚିହ୍ନଇ କି?
title: A fine shawl and forgotten faces
literal_meaning: Is this the former Kahnei? With a fine soft shawl on the shoulder, does he recognise people?
explanation: The question contrasts a remembered person with the way he now behaves. The fine shawl becomes the visible sign beside a failure to recognise others. Our reading hears a teasing accusation that improved appearance or standing has brought social distance. The line does not tell us that the cloth itself changes character, or that everyone whose circumstances improve becomes proud. Its force is directed at the particular person being addressed through this pointed question.
meaning_odia: ଏ କି ସେଇ ପୂର୍ବର କହ୍ନେଇ—ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ପୁରୁଣା ପରିଚୟ ଓ ଏବର ଆଚରଣ ମୁହାଁମୁହିଁ ହେଉଛି। କାନ୍ଧର ସରୁ କୋମଳ ଚାଦର ପାଖରେ ମଣିଷ ନ ଚିହ୍ନିବାର କଥା ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ବେଶ ବା ସ୍ଥିତି ବଦଳିଲା ପରେ ପୁରୁଣା ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଅବହେଳା କରିବା ଉପରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ପୋଷାକଟି ନିଜେ ଦୋଷୀ ନୁହେଁ; ତାହା ପିନ୍ଧିଥିବା ଲୋକର ବ୍ୟବହାର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ପଡ଼ୁଛି।
english_summary: A changed appearance becomes an image for forgetting familiar people.
odia_summary: ବେଶ ବଦଳିଲା ପରେ ପରିଚିତ ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଭୁଲିବାରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: After a promotion, a friend stops greeting the people who used to share lunch with him. One of them quotes the saying in a private conversation, teasing the new distance rather than the friend’s clothes.
cultural_context: The source labels the headword Jajpur; no exclusive origin follows. Kahnei remains the name in the quotation, not an identified deity or historical person. Fine soft cloth is explicit; fibre, cost and status-history are not established. Source spelling ପୂରୂବ retained.

odia: ପରଧନେ ଲହର ଫହର; ଛଡାଇ ନେଲେ ଲାଜେ ମର
title: A flourish on someone else’s wealth
literal_meaning: You move about in style on another’s wealth; when it is taken away, you die of shame.
explanation: The first half gives someone room to move and make a show; the second suddenly takes that support away. The dictionary defines the headword as moving to and fro, while the verse puts that movement on another person’s wealth. Read as a taunt, it catches the embarrassment of displaying what one cannot claim as one’s own. The closing “die of shame” is exaggerated reproach, not a literal instruction. Our wider reading concerns borrowed display and insecure pretension, not the worth of people who receive help.
meaning_odia: ପରର ଧନରେ ଚାଲିଛି ଲହର ଫହର; ସେ ଧନ ଫେରିଗଲେ ଦେଖାଣିର ଭିତ୍ତିଟି ମଧ୍ୟ ରହେନାହିଁ। ପ୍ରଥମ ଭାଗର ଆରାମ ଓ ଚଳପ୍ରଚଳକୁ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଭାଗର ଲାଜ ହଠାତ୍ ଅଟକାଇଦିଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ନିଜର ନୁହେଁ ଏମିତି ଜିନିଷକୁ ନିଜ ବଡ଼ପଣର ପ୍ରମାଣ କରି ଦେଖାଇବା ଏହି ଟାହିର ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ। “ଲାଜେ ମର” କଥାର ଅତିରଞ୍ଜନ; ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ନେଉଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ଛୋଟ କରିବା ଏଠାରେ ଆମର ପଢ଼ା ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: Borrowed display can become embarrassment when its support is withdrawn.
odia_summary: ପରର ଧନରେ ନିଜ ବଡ଼ପଣ ଦେଖାଇଲେ, ତାହା ଫେରିଗଲେ ଲାଜରେ ପଡ଼ିବାର ଟାହି।
usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone poses with a friend’s expensive camera and lets others think it belongs to them. When the friend asks for it back, another friend quotes the saying softly. The joke concerns the false impression, not borrowing a camera.
cultural_context: The dictionary labels the headword Sambalpur; this is a source label, not proof of exclusive regional origin. The display reading is editorial close reading, not an independently supplied traditional-use gloss.

odia: ବୋହି ଗଲା ପାଣି ଯାଉ ତେଣିକି, ବନ୍ଧେଇଲା ପାଣି ରହୁ ଅଟକି
title: What has flowed, what remains
literal_meaning: Let the water that has flowed away go that way; let the dammed water remain held.
explanation: The two wishes face different water: what has already gone and what can remain contained. Our reading turns attention from recovering every loss to keeping what is still available. This is an editorial application of the contrast, not a promise that every loss can be repaired by restraint.
meaning_odia: ଦୁଇଟି ଇଚ୍ଛା ଦୁଇ ଅବସ୍ଥାର ପାଣିକୁ ନେଇ—ଯାହା ବୋହିଗଲା ଓ ଯାହା ଅଟକି ରହିଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ହରାଇଥିବା ଜିନିଷ ଫେରାଇବାଠାରୁ ଧ୍ୟାନ ଏବେ ଥିବା ଜିନିଷକୁ ରଖିବା ଆଡ଼କୁ ଫେରେ। ଏହା ବିରୋଧଟିର ଆମର ପ୍ରୟୋଗ; ସଂଯମରେ ସବୁ କ୍ଷତି ଭରଣା ହେବ ବୋଲି ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: Our reading distinguishes a past loss from what can still be kept.
odia_summary: ବିତିଥିବା କ୍ଷତି ଓ ରଖିପାରିବା ଜିନିଷ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଆମ ପଢ଼ାର ତଫାତ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ବର୍ଷାରେ ପଢ଼ାଚକ୍ରର ଗୋଟିଏ ଦିନ ବାତିଲ ହେଲା। ଆୟୋଜକ ସେଦିନକୁ ନେଇ ଅନୁତାପ କରୁଥିବାବେଳେ ସାଙ୍ଗ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇ କହିଲେ, “ଆସନ୍ତା ଦୁଇଦିନର ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥା କରିବା।” / Rain cancels one day of a reading programme. While an organiser regrets it, a friend recalls the saying: “Let us arrange the two days still ahead.” This application is invented.
cultural_context: The verb’s dam-building sense supports the water image. No particular river, engineering method, conservation custom or practical water-management instruction is documented here.

title: Borrowing and answering for another
literal_meaning: I would borrow, but would not become surety for someone else.
explanation: The dictionary’s inline explanation distinguishes taking a loan from guaranteeing another person. The first-person voice accepts one involvement and refuses the other. Our reading hears a boundary between bearing one’s own obligation and answering for someone else; it does not turn that preference into a rule everyone should follow.
meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନର ସଂଲଗ୍ନ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଋଣ ନେବା ଓ ଅନ୍ୟ ପାଇଁ ଜାମିନ ହେବାକୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ। ବକ୍ତା ଗୋଟିଏ ସମ୍ପର୍କରେ ପଶିବାକୁ ମାନେ, ଅନ୍ୟଟିକୁ ମନା କରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ନିଜ ଦାୟ ନେବା ଓ ପର ପାଇଁ ଉତ୍ତରଦାୟୀ ହେବା ମଧ୍ୟରେ ସୀମା ଶୁଣାଯାଏ; ସେ ପସନ୍ଦ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ନିୟମ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Our reading hears a speaker distinguishing two kinds of obligation.
odia_summary: ଦୁଇ ପ୍ରକାର ଦାୟକୁ ଅଲଗା କରୁଥିବା ବକ୍ତାକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ଶୁଣେ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “କଥାଟିରେ ଋଣଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ଦାୟର ଭେଦ ମୋତେ ଶୁଣାଯାଉଛି।” ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ପଚାରିଲେ, “ନିଜ ପାଇଁ କହିବା ଓ ପର ପାଇଁ କଥା ଦେବା କି ଏକା?” / A reading group discusses the difference between speaking for oneself and giving one’s word for someone else. This discussion is invented, not borrowing advice.
